purpose: Close the temporary early-March US fast-deck compression by adjudicating Lexington CV-16 branch repair return and Hornet CV-12 arrival while retaining long-repair/new-build guards.

Lexington_CV16.branch_damage_clock: GALVANIC branch repair band 1944-03-10..25 due torpedo plus bomb/flight-deck damage, deliberately slower than historical torpedo-only case.
Lexington_CV16.reason: Use mid-band repair completion plus Pacific transit/reintegration; no reason to hold to the late edge absent a new yard complication.
Lexington_CV16.historical_sanity_anchor: Historical Lexington repairs were completed 20 Feb and she was at Majuro by 8 Mar; Branch return is therefore intentionally later because Branch damage was heavier.

Hornet_CV12.historical_anchor: Historical Hornet joined the Fast Carrier Task Force at Majuro on 20 Mar 1944; no Branch event delays her construction/shakedown/transit.

strategic_effect: The Japanese early-March temporary deck-count window is effectively closed by 20 Mar. US fast-battleship/radar/CIC advantages were never absent, so this is reinforcement of an already dangerous fleet system rather than recovery from collapse.
